newsitem.title: USA: U.S. House panel delays budget amendment vote.
newsitem.headline: U.S. House panel delays budget amendment vote.

text.p: House Judiciary Committee chairman Henry Hyde abruptly postponed until Feb. 11 the panel's vote on the Republican-backed balanced budget constitutional amemdment.

The Illinois Republican's announcement came as a surprise to committee members. An aide said it there were questions as to whether enough Republican members would be present at the vote Wednesday to be assured they would defeat a proposed Democratic change to exempt Social Security funds.
Republicans control the committee 25-15. "You still have to have the members there," the aide said. An estimated dozen proposals to change the amendment are expected.

Democrat John Conyers of Michigan offered the proposed change which many in his party believe would protect Social Security from extreme cuts in the next century when the trust fund stops growing. The rest of the government now borrows from the fund's surpluses but when large numbers of the baby-boom generation begin to retire, the fund will need to be repaid.

Republicans countered that by exempting Social Security from the balanced budget, Washington would be more likely to cut other programs that aid senior citizens including Medicare. "If you don't balance the budget there is no hope for Social Security," Rep. Bob Ingliss, Republican of South Carolina said.
The Senate is to begin voting on the amendment to the U.S. Constitution Wednesday afternoon but no vote is expected until late in the month. The House is to vote on it Feb. 26.
The House passed the amendment in 1995 but it failed in the Senate that year by one vote. Votes in both chambers this year are expected to be very close.
It would require the budget be balanced every year during peacetime and would make it more difficult to approve deficit spending, raise taxes and increase the public debt.
